corrections.new:
THE SEAM, NOT THE PROVIDERS. `gcp_kms_keysource.rs`, `aws_kms_keysource.rs` and `aws_sts.rs`
are the adapters BENEATH this seam and belong to no unit; nothing here establishes that any
of them speaks its provider's protocol correctly, selects the right key, or reaches the
endpoint a deployment intended. What is established is that whatever they return crosses this
boundary only as a typed value the seam could construct, and only after verifying.

NOT A CLAIM ABOUT KEY CUSTODY. That the private key never leaves the KMS is the provider's
property and the trait's shape — this trait never asks for a private key — not a result
proved here.

NOT A CLAIM ABOUT THE FAILURE PATH. How a failed remote-signer call is classified, and
whether it arms the handshake-path throttle, is `remote_signer_call`'s authority. It has no
unit, it is gated on `any(aws_kms_keysource, gcp_kms_keysource)` — the shape that makes a
single-feature lane silent about the other — and it is recorded as a named gap rather than
absorbed here.

The public-key rule itself is NOT implemented here: what makes a blob a legal Ed25519 public
key is a property of the key representation with its own owner under ADR-MCPRE-063 Slice 2,
and this seam maps that owner's refusal into the `KeyError` vocabulary its callers match on.
The three distinctions that owner draws — unreadable bytes, a well-formed key of another
algorithm, a non-canonical encoding — are rendered into the message rather than lost, because
this vocabulary has one variant for all three.

Executable, class V0, measured in the default Bazel lane (`bazel test //...`). Outside every root's closure: no
root's response-signing claim is stated at this seam, and the delegated-signing terminal that
roots consume is `proxy.delegated_signing_credential`'s.

corrections.new:
NOT A CUSTODY CLAIM. That the private key never leaves the KMS or the token is the provider's
property and the trait's shape — none of these traits asks for a private key — and it is not
proved here. In particular NOTHING here is a FIPS-140-2 Level 3 or HSM-protection claim: a
Cloud KMS EC_SIGN_ED25519 key version may be SOFTWARE- or HSM-protected and the two REST
operations used cannot establish which, so the KMS adapters are honestly labelled
software-protection custody. Real FIPS-L3 custody evidence remains a DEFERRED obligation
awaiting validated hardware.

NOT A PROTOCOL-CONFORMANCE CLAIM. That each adapter speaks its provider's wire protocol
correctly is established by its own controls against fixtures, not against a live provider;
the live-infra lane is separate and off the merge path.

NOT THE ENDPOINT RULE ITSELF. Which endpoints an operator may set is THM-0089's; what is
established here is that each adapter consults it and refuses at construction.

NOT THE SEAM'S TYPES. `RawEd25519Message`, `RawEd25519Signature` and `Ed25519SpkiDer` are
THM-0108's, and the seam's re-verification is kept as defence in depth beneath these adapters'
own.

THREE LANES, MEASURED SEPARATELY. Each adapter exists only under its own non-default feature;
the crate's default-feature test targets compile all three to zero tests, so each is its own unit
naming its own lane.

Executable, class V0, measured in the three named feature lanes.
